items.title: Making “A Post-Pandemic World” — Jake Glanville
items.why: A long technical interview on why seasonal flu vaccines need constant updating, how influenza infects a cell, and why broadly neutralizing antibodies are rare. The universal-vaccine program is the CEO's own account, so treat its promise as unverified; the immunology explanation is the main value.
items.takeaway: The interview cites seasonal flu vaccine efficacy of roughly 15 to 60 percent. It describes the company's vaccine as tested in about 180 people and heading toward Phase 2, which are company-reported claims.

items.title: Great Leaps in Biological Theory
items.why: Traces how two major theories, chemiosmotic coupling and clonal selection, were proposed before direct experimental evidence. It looks at the reasoning behind the leaps, which is useful for thinking about theory in biology.
items.takeaway: The essay argues that Mitchell's and Jerne's philosophical commitments helped them break from the prevailing frameworks.

items.title: AlphaFold @ CASP13: “What just happened?”
items.why: A critical firsthand assessment of AlphaFold at CASP13 that separates the science from the hype. It weighs the significance of the result against CASP's historical progress and metrics, and explains the method as a distance-distribution potential minimised by gradient descent. It is a 2018 view, written before the DeepMind paper was out.
items.takeaway: The author estimates the advance at roughly two CASPs' worth of progress, and cautions that global GDT metrics can hide local accuracy.

items.title: Protein Linguistics
items.why: The author of RGN explains the motivation for an end-to-end differentiable structure model, including the 'linguistic hypothesis' about reusable protein fragments. It is a hypothesis-driven account from an unfamiliar angle, and the author is open about the early preprint's limits.

items.title: Learning the integral of a diffusion model
items.why: Explains flow maps, networks that predict any point on a diffusion path from any other point, and organises the many training variants.
items.takeaway: Deterministic diffusion sampling gives unique, non-crossing paths between noise and data, and flow maps learn to jump along those paths.

items.title: Perspectives on diffusion
items.why: A clear tour of the equivalent views of diffusion (autoencoders, latent-variable models, score matching, SDEs, flow-based models). It is the background the flow-maps post assumes, and the author says it is meant to build intuition rather than be fully rigorous.

items.title: Calculus on Computational Graphs: Backpropagation
items.why: Colah's classic explanation of backpropagation as reverse-mode differentiation on computational graphs. It covers why the cost scales with outputs rather than inputs, which also underlies scientific computing and differentiable models.
items.takeaway: Reverse mode gives the derivative of one output with respect to all inputs in a single pass, which is why it is so much cheaper than forward mode for training.

items.title: Branch Specialization
items.why: An interpretability article on how neurons cluster into functional groups across network branches, shown through AlexNet and InceptionV1 with feature visualisation. It is a large-scale structure finding, tied to the Circuits thread's approach rather than a general claim.

items.title: Characterising nanobody developability to improve therapeutic design using the Therapeutic Nanobody Profiler
items.why: Introduces an open-source tool, with code and a web app, for assessing nanobody developability. It benchmarks candidates against 36 clinical-stage nanobodies and adds assay data on 108 nanobodies. The excerpt is a short pointer to the published paper, so read the paper for the evidence.
items.takeaway: The tool uses 6 metrics tailored to nanobodies; the code and datasets are open source.

items.title: OAS-nano: New Repertoire Database Just Dropped
items.why: Describes a processed database of natural nanobody (VHH) repertoires aimed at antibody language models. The post spells out its pipeline choices, such as germline assignment and amplification protocols, and what they mean for bias when building training sets.
items.takeaway: After deduplication it contains 73 million sequences, which the authors say is 5x the largest previous resource under the same redundancy filter.
